entities.label: Movement
entities.summary:
Public administration is a modern movement that has shaped the world's governance since the 18th century. Its significance lies in the establishment of the bureaucratic system, which has influenced the development of politics, economy, and society globally. The core events of public administration include the French Revolution's emphasis on merit-based appointments, the rise of the British Civil Service, and the creation of the US Department of State in 1789. These events produced the modern concept of public administration as a professional field, which has since become a cornerstone of modern governance.

The legacy of public administration can be seen in the establishment of the United Nations and the European Union, which have formalized international cooperation and European integration. The movement's influence on the development of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law has also been profound. One striking statistic is that over 90% of countries in the world have a public administration system in place.

One vivid closing is 'The public administration movement has created a culture of professionalism, which has transformed the way governments operate and interact with their citizens.'
